title: OpenAI ships three real-time audio models for voice agents
meta_description: OpenAI launched three real-time audio models aimed at conversational agents, live translation, and transcription, pushing voice from a feature toward core infrastructure.
tldr: OpenAI released three real-time audio models targeting conversational agents, translation, and transcription. The split into purpose-built models signals that voice is being treated as production infrastructure for agents rather than a single bolt-on speech feature.
body_markdown:
## What launched

OpenAI introduced **three real-time audio models**, each pointed at a distinct job: powering conversational agents, performing live translation, and handling transcription. Rather than one general speech model, the lineup splits voice into specialized building blocks that developers can compose.

## Why three models, not one

Voice workloads pull in different directions. A conversational agent needs low latency and natural turn-taking; translation needs accuracy across languages and faithful meaning under time pressure; transcription needs robustness to noise and speaker variety. Shipping separate, real-time models lets teams optimize for the constraint that actually matters in their product instead of compromising across all three.

## The bigger trend

The release fits the dominant June 2026 theme of AI moving toward **agents and real-world execution**. Real-time audio is a core dependency for that: an agent that can listen, respond, translate, and transcribe in the moment is far more useful in support, accessibility, and live collaboration than one limited to text. Treating audio as infrastructure, with low-latency primitives, is what makes those experiences feel responsive rather than laggy.

## What to watch

Key questions for builders are end-to-end latency under real network conditions, language coverage and quality for the translation model, pricing for always-on streaming workloads, and how cleanly the three models hand off to each other inside a single agent loop.

faq.question: What are the three audio models for?
faq.answer: OpenAI positioned them for three jobs: powering conversational agents, real-time translation, and transcription. Each is tuned for the constraints of its task rather than being a single general-purpose speech model.

faq.question: Why does real-time matter for voice agents?
faq.answer: Latency is what makes a voice interaction feel natural. Real-time models reduce the delay between speaking and responding, which is essential for agents handling live support, accessibility, or translation.

faq.question: Can the models be combined?
faq.answer: The lineup is designed as composable building blocks, so an agent can transcribe, reason, translate, and speak using the appropriate model for each step. Hand-off behavior in a single loop is something developers will want to test.
